subject: exercise-sports-science
title: Energy Systems: Three Systems Sharing One Bout

segments.say: All three systems switch on together. In the first seconds ATP-PC holds the largest share at 70 percent while the phosphocreatine store is full, glycolysis already supplies 20 percent and the aerobic system 10 percent. Point at the three bars on your student notes diagram before any share changes.
questions: Which system holds the largest share in the first seconds, and how large is it?
Are any of the three systems switched off at the start of the bout?

segments.say: The phosphocreatine store drains and ATP-PC fades. By about 10 seconds ATP-PC is down to 35 percent, glycolysis has risen to 40 percent and the aerobic share is 25 percent. Now try the share questions on your worksheet.
questions: Why does the ATP-PC share fall as the bout continues?
What are the three shares at about 10 seconds?

segments.say: Glycolysis takes the largest share as lactate builds. At about 30 seconds glycolysis holds 55 percent, the aerobic share has climbed to 35 percent and ATP-PC is down to 10 percent but still contributing. Check the lactate marker against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Which system holds the largest share at about 30 seconds, and what builds up as it works?
How has the aerobic share changed since the first seconds?

segments.say: The aerobic system ramps up to dominate. Minutes in it supplies 75 percent, while glycolysis still supplies 20 percent and ATP-PC 5 percent. Keep the together, fade, peak, dominate order as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: Which system dominates minutes into the bout, and do the other two still contribute?
What are the four stages of the handover, in order?
segments.watchFor: The body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out. Listen for students who switch a system fully off when its share falls, or start a system only when another runs out. Send them back to scene 2 and the three shares at 10 seconds - 35, 40 and 25 percent: All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes as the bout continues - ATP-PC fades as the phosphocreatine store drains, anaerobic glycolysis peaks as lactate builds, and the aerobic system rises to dominate longer work.
